contexts.correctionCheck: The primary PDF, PubMed/Europe PMC metadata and exact DOI correction, erratum and retraction searches were checked on 14 September 2026. No notice resolving the stated reporting conflicts was identified. This is not exhaustive correction surveillance.
contexts.finding: Early neuronal-appearing labels and later nonneuronal profiles coexist with an adult neuronal-detection null. Repeated doses, shared specimens and separate phenotype assays cannot establish a universal cessation or memory mechanism.
limitations: Eighteen rhesus monkeys span E140 to seventeen years: seventeen receive autoradiography and one E144 animal is used only for electron-microscopic GFAP. Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. This is evidence of overlapping material, pending original identity confirmation. Shared juvenile identifiers also have discordant age/survival reporting: 030783 is P149-P184 here versus seven months at death in 1985; 031683 is P507-P549 and six weeks here versus nineteen months and thirty-five days. Neither independent pooling nor silent record merging is justified.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

GFAP immunochemistry uses 30-micrometre vibratome sections from five animals. Antibody penetration reaches only about three micrometres. The normal-goat-serum primary-antibody control is incubated at 4 degrees C, whereas primary antiserum incubation is at room temperature. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

Postnatal short-interval and longer-survival groups contain different animals. Approximately 150 sections across three longer-survival ages yielded eight profiles classified morphologically as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. These are sampled profiles, not eight animals, a clonal lineage or a daily birth rate; Nissl morphology has acknowledged identity limits.

The P149-P184 interval is thirty-five days/five weeks in Table 1 and text, but Figure 4B says six weeks. Figure 5 uses P507-P549. Neither is an adult cohort. The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

GFAP composition in Figures 7-10 concerns small SGZ cells without birth-label selection. The E144 animal was never thymidine-labeled; about half its sampled small cells are GFAP-positive. Approximately 75% at six months and a majority at later ages do not quantify the astrocytic fraction of adult newborn cells or prove two founder lineages.

The combined electron-microscopic assay examined 120 ultrathin semiserial sections from selected areas in each of three animals aged six months, one and a half years, and five years. A dozen reliably radiolabeled cells were found, six GFAP-positive. This is a pooled three-age subset, not twelve adult neurons or a representative adult astrocyte fraction. Figure 11 is juvenile; Figure 12 is the five-year-old animal.

Figure 12B is described as an oligodendroglial type in Results but as resting microglia in the caption. Its specific subtype remains unresolved. No labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses in the examined sections; this sampling-limited null does not prove absence of all neuronal precursor potential.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

A 1/4/24-hour comparison across sacrificed cohorts does not demonstrate persistence in the same cell, lifelong memory, inheritance or a universal minimal assembly. RNA abundance is distinct from transcription rate, protein output and behavioral function.

Figure 6c has a 144/114 gene-count conflict. Figure 7c caption says E0/E4/E24, while plot and experimental text specify E0/E1/E4. Supplementary Tables 4-5 contain conflicting headers, nonfinite values or spreadsheet errors. No global quantitative model is calibrated from these data.

limitations: The abstract's four macrocomponents and the body's three grouped components are different groupings of the proposed architecture. Neither yields a measured carrier count, calibrated dependency weight or validated graph-generation rule. A selective causal assay must define whether its outcome is recognition, felt sharing, perspective taking or helping.

Perceptual access to social information does not establish one universal visual or multisensory mechanism. The review includes observed, imagined and narrated situations; no selective test makes one perception node necessary for all of them.

Affective sharing is part of this attributed definition, but a definition does not prove a necessary dependency on every affect-generation process. Recognition, concern, personal distress, felt sharing and helping are different outcomes.

Working memory, inhibitory control and mentalizing are not interchangeable. Pages 82 and 86 describe dissociations between executive-task and theory-of-mind impairments; these secondary summaries require primary review before any specific lesion effect is admitted. They do not calibrate a universal maintenance dependency.

Page 91 states that the proposed psychological constructs are not primitive and still need decomposition. There is no fixed cardinality, measured carrier threshold or numerical weighting of perception, affect and control. Frontal activation can reflect inhibition or monitoring/manipulation of internally generated information; neither is uniquely established by the review.

limitations: Approximately three-month-old male Arc-CreERT2/R26R-eYFP mice on a C57BL/6J background. Training includes a tone paired with footshock in a context; the changed-context comparison alters several environmental cues. It is not a context-only learning protocol or an isolated chromatin intervention.

Basal denotes NeuN+/eYFP- nuclei collected after training, not naive home-cage animals. Early denotes NeuN+/eYFP+ at 1.5-2 hours, Late the tagged population at five days without recall, and Reactivated NeuN+/eYFP+/Arc+ after re-exposure in a different cohort. Marker selection, reporter maturation and a roughly 12-hour labeling window limit cell identity and temporal specificity.

Whole-hippocampus molecular samples pool nuclei across animals and neuronal subtypes. ATAC Methods specify 10,000 nuclei from 8-10 mice per replicate. Table 13 lists three Basal and four Late libraries, while the reporting summary excludes one Basal from 13 and Figure 2a states n=3 per group. The included-library mapping remains unresolved. A library, genomic locus, slice or punctum is not an independent animal. Destructive cohorts are not single-cell longitudinal measurements.

Figure 1f counts are labeled cells per DG slice; the caption refers to hippocampus. Its five versus six mice each contribute six sections, while tests report df=59/57. Extended Data 1e gives n=15 with df=14 without a clear per-group denominator; 1c has n=30 with df=16. Animal-level effects and confidence intervals require source measurements and sample reconciliation.

Hi-C Methods describe two libraries per Basal, Early and Late population, but the reporting summary excludes one Early library. Methods say two animals per sample, whereas reporting specifies four to five. Promoter-capture Hi-C covers four populations and selected promoters. Contact frequencies and inferred A/B compartments are not unique three-dimensional coordinates. Figure 3 specifies a 500-kb Juicer representation, while Methods and software use 50-kb HOMER compartment PCA; their mapping needs explicit reconstruction.

ATAC Figure 2a labels log2 fold-change thresholds, while its caption, Methods and software say fold changes >1.5. RNA Table 8 has undocumented sign reorientation and a near-threshold extra row. The RNA Methods cite an edgeR reference for DESeq2 and the software omits the RNA export code. No sequence analysis, signed gene-specific pathway or edge weight is calibrated.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues. Sequencing sample sizes used observed variability and group differences; ATAC/Hi-C quality exclusions and a plotted ATAC outlier exclusion were not pre-established. Normality was assumed without formal testing. Null tests are not equivalence tests. Separate molecular profiles and behavioral outcomes do not establish a chromatin-to-memory mediation chain or lifelong persistence.

eIF4E and GRIA1 puncta measure protein immunoreactivity, not translation rate, receptor current or synaptic efficacy. The Results/caption call the measured shaft dendritic, but Figure 5f labels an axon and Methods describe axon surfaces; exact compartment identity and distance units require clarification. Sections and neurites are nested within mice.

Reported group randomization and selected blinded quantification do not resolve all sampling issues.
